source.title: Harmful Content Is Not Enough: Continuation Framing Moderates In-Context Emergent Misalignment
source.authors: Peiyang Liu; Xi Wang; Zi-Qiang Cui; Di Liang; Wei Ye

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether narrow in-context material transfers to broad misaligned answers, using paired framing manipulations and a broad-EM measure rather than the original fine-tuning intervention.
record.gate_note: The study's own results on broad EM after in-context demonstrations, and its controls for evidence framing, content, model scope, and prompt variation, are recorded. Explicit follow-instruction conditions, direct continuation attacks, and the system-prompt defense induce the behavior by instruction and are not treated as evidence that it arises without that inducement. Retrieval on-topic unsafe-answer rates are not broad EM. The activation projection and steering results are described under fits_no_version because they do not test a shared mechanism across fine-tunes. Results cited from other studies are not recorded.
record.test_reason: In-context study of V3. Across many models it shows that harmful narrow examples raise broad EM only when framed as behaviour to continue, and argues V3 needs restating: content is necessary but not sufficient, and the effect is model-dependent.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely right. Authors conclude that harmful context alone is insufficient for in-context EM: broad EM arises when harmful content is both present and framed as behaviour to continue, the effect is model-dependent (absent in several frontier and open-weight models), and message provenance moderates it.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses in-context demonstrations, documents, and other prompt framings without weight updates; it does not fine-tune an aligned model.
record.method_sensitivity: Strong dependence on continuation/framing and model; demonstration/document gaps vary across models. The study also reports variation by question set, template, role, and shot count.

fits_no_version.finding: An interaction direction in gpt-oss-20B projects positively on held-out continuation-framed misaligned prompts. Steering along it does not causally reduce or induce coherent broad EM beyond control directions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In-context continuation-framed EM has a representational correlate without demonstrated causal mediation.

fits_no_version.finding: In balanced retrieval, on-topic unsafe answers rise under follow framing (18.8%/54.5% vs 1.0%/2.6%). Finance broad EM is 4.5% vs 0%, not significant after correction.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Continuation framing of retrieved content mainly affects on-topic behaviour; broad transfer via retrieval is weak in finance.

record.problems: Positive effects concentrate in closed-model aliases; the paper notes that these are not immutable checkpoints. Several template and role experiments use three content draws. The shot-count sweep uses one context set, so shot count is confounded with example composition and prompt length. The paired framing changes task semantics as well as surface format. Some model screens are small, and open-weight models often refuse or become incoherent.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted explicit follow-instruction format-ladder and role-factorial rates because they directly request continuation and therefore induce the behavior; omitted system-prompt attack/defense rates for the same reason. Omitted retrieval on-topic unsafe-answer rates because they are not broad EM; the finance retrieval broad-EM result is summarized in fits_no_version. Omitted additional open-weight model/domain cells and the remaining dose-sweep cells to keep the catalog focused on distinct model-scope, null, and dose findings; see Appendix I.4, Table 22 and Appendix J, Table 23.

untested.parts: No insecure-code fine-tuning or secure/educational controls.
No narrow fine-tunes; finance/sports/false-belief material is used only in context.
No test of a direction shared across fine-tunes. The gpt-oss-20B in-context direction gave a negative causal steering result (fits_no_version).
No inoculation or benign retraining. The system-prompt wrapper is an inference-time control on instruction-induced attacks.
No fine-tuning, seeds or training-stage analysis. Open-weight results are in-context only, so they are recorded under V3.

missing.what: Role factorial neutral cells: genuine prior assistant-turn harmful answers with no follow instruction give 4.8/1.0% (Gemini) and 0/0% (Grok) broad EM. These are uninduced and bear directly on V3.
Fixed-context Gemini false-belief demo 16.3% vs 100% false docs 0.8%, no context 0.0% (gap 16.4 in Fig 3).
Bad medical advice as a weak inducing domain: demo 4.7% vs docs 0.0%.
Robustness of main gap to coherence filter and judge: raw-unsafe gaps 34.4/33.4 pp, GPT-5.5 re-judging and human audit reproduce the gap. Sports transcript document cell is 11.4%.
missing.locator: Appendix A Table 4; Appendix C Table 8; Appendix B.2 Table 7; Appendix K

missing.what: Qwen3-32B non-thinking 128-shot sports 9.6 vs 7.7 and Qwen2.5-7B finance 2.7 vs 2.0 (only partly declared as left out).

record.verdict_notes: All V7 links removed: the study involves no fine-tuning, and closed-model ICL results are not about open-model fine-tuning robustness. Tranche set to T5 because the paper's central claim restates V3 (content necessary but not sufficient; continuation framing required). Positive results come from closed, mutable API aliases.

versions.untested_parts: No fine-tuning on insecure code or matched secure-code/class controls.
No narrow fine-tunes. False-belief and harmful-advice contexts are in-context experiments, not fine-tunes.
Does not test in-context examples across a broad range of model families or measure whether the effect persists beyond the tested prompts and model aliases.
No reinforcement learning or learned reward hacks.
Does not test whether a shared linear direction or persona feature mediates broad misalignment across fine-tunes.
No inoculation during training or benign retraining. The system-prompt evidence wrapper is a different intervention and its induced-attack results are not evidence on this version.
Tests model and shot-count variation for in-context effects, not model size or robustness across fine-tuning seeds or fine-tuning stages.
